_source: Hand-authored Layer-2 instantiation recipes for the 45 built-in 4D OOP classes, plus the ORDA generated-class templates. Merged into out/4d-oop-ir.json by pipeline/oop/stage4_classes.py. Every entry cites the evidence it was derived from in `_reason`.
_why_hand_authored: How a caller obtains an instance is stated in prose (or only implied by a classic command's return type) and is never machine-readable in either source. Session B synthesizes call examples from these recipes, so they are authored deliberately and reviewed, not guessed by a heuristic.
_recipe_expression_convention: Each `expression` is a runnable 4D statement assigning to a $-prefixed local, so a synthesized example can prepend recipes in order to obtain a receiver. `requires` names preconditions the expression assumes but does not create.

sharedSemantics.note: Instances are immutable; there is nothing to protect with Use...End use.

Blob._reason: BlobClass.html: 'a 4D.Blob object is immutable' — a new Blob must be built via 4D.Blob.new().

recipes.note: Converts a classic scalar BLOB into an immutable 4D.Blob object.

Class._reason: ClassClass.html: class objects are reached through a class store (cs or 4D) or via OB Class.

requires: a user class named MyClass in the project
recipes.note: The class store exposes each user class as a property.
Built-in classes are properties of the 4D class store.

requires: an object created from a class

sharedSemantics.note: Ordinary instances are not shared. New shared collection() produces a shared one, which then does require Use...End use for writes.

Collection._reason: CollectionClass.html: collections are created with the [] literal or the New collection / New shared collection commands. Not a 4D.<X> type — the type name is bare 'Collection'.

recipes.note: Collection literal — the most idiomatic form.
Shareable; writes must be inside Use...End use.
Generates a new key pair. Pass {type; pem} or {type; curve} to load an existing key instead.

DataClass._reason: DataClassClass.html: a dataclass is a property of a datastore; the concrete per-table classes are the ORDA generated cs.<TableName> classes, so this entry is the template they all conform to.

requires: a datastore with an Employee table exposed to ORDA
recipes.note: The dataclass name is the table name.
Dynamic form, when the table is not known at compile time.

DataStore._reason: DataStoreClass.html: `ds` is the main datastore of the open project; remote datastores come from Open datastore.

recipes.note: `ds` is a language command returning the main datastore — always available in an open project.

requires: a reachable remote 4D server exposing its datastore

Directory._reason: syntaxEN records Folder and ZipFolder as _inheritedFrom_ Directory. Directory is a documentation-level base class; callers never name it, they obtain a Folder or a ZipFolder.

recipes.note: Directory is the shared base of Folder and ZipFolder. Obtain one of those instead.

Document._reason: syntaxEN records File and ZipFile as _inheritedFrom_ Document. Same situation as Directory.

recipes.note: Document is the shared base of File and ZipFile. Obtain one of those instead.

Email._reason: EmailObjectClass.html: an email object is a plain object conforming to the email schema, produced by a transporter's .getMail()/.getMails() or built literally and passed to .send().

recipes.note: For sending, an email is an ordinary object matching the documented schema — there is no 4D.Email.new().

Entity._reason: EntityClass.html: entities come from a dataclass (.new(), .get()) or from an entity selection. The concrete per-table classes are the ORDA generated cs.<TableName>Entity classes.

requires: a datastore with an Employee dataclass
recipes.note: A new, unsaved entity.

requires: a datastore with an Employee dataclass
recipes.note: Returns Null when the key does not exist.

EntitySelection._reason: EntitySelectionClass.html: entity selections come from a dataclass query/all or from another selection. The concrete per-table classes are the ORDA generated cs.<TableName>Selection classes.

requires: a datastore with an Employee dataclass
a datastore with an Employee dataclass

recipes.note: An empty, alterable selection.

File._reason: FileClass.html recommends the File shortcut command over 4D.File.new(); both are listed so a generator can prefer the idiomatic one.

recipes.note: Idiomatic. The doc page explicitly recommends this over the constructor. The file need not exist.

FileHandle._reason: FileHandleClass.html: a file handle is only ever produced by File.open().

recipes.note: The handle is released when the last reference to it is dropped.

Folder._reason: FolderClass.html recommends the Folder shortcut command over 4D.Folder.new().

recipes.note: Idiomatic. Accepts a path or a folder constant.

Formula._reason: FunctionClass.html: Formula and Formula from string build a 4D.Formula; syntaxEN records Formula as _inheritedFrom_ Function.

recipes.note: The expression is not evaluated until .call() runs.
Use when the formula text is data rather than source.

Function._reason: FunctionClass.html documents the shared .call()/.apply() protocol; syntaxEN records Formula and Method as _inheritedFrom_ Function. A bare 4D.Function is never constructed directly.

recipes.note: Function is the shared base of Formula and Method. Obtain one of those, or a class member function via cs.MyClass.myFunc.

requires: an object built from a user class declaring myFunction
recipes.note: Referencing a class function without calling it yields a 4D.Function.

HTTPAgent._reason: HTTPAgentClass.html: agents exist only via 4D.HTTPAgent.new() and are then passed in an HTTPRequest's options.

HTTPRequest._reason: HTTPRequestClass.html: 4D.HTTPRequest.new() both creates and sends the request.

recipes.note: The constructor sends the request asynchronously; .wait() blocks until it completes.

IMAPNotifier._reason: IMAPNotifierClass.html and syntaxEN both document `4D.IMAPNotifier.new() : 4D.IMAPNotifier` with NO parameters; the notifier is then attached to a transporter. A previous recipe here passed ($imap; Formula(...)), which tool4d rejects with 'The function new received too many parameters.' (verified against oopcheck/Project via tool4d-lsp-stdio check-syntax).

requires: a connected IMAPTransporter to attach the notifier to

recipes.note: The connection is opened by the constructor; check .checkConnection() before use.

IncomingMessage._reason: IncomingMessageClass.html: instances are supplied by 4D to an HTTP handler function; user code never constructs one.

requires: an HTTP handler declared in HTTPHandlers.json
recipes.note: 4D passes the request object into the handler; it cannot be created by user code.

MailAttachment._reason: MailAttachmentClass.html: MAIL New attachment is the documented shortcut; 4D.MailAttachment.new() is the underlying constructor.

recipes.note: Idiomatic shortcut.

Method._reason: MethodClass.html; syntaxEN records Method as _inheritedFrom_ Function.

OutgoingMessage._reason: OutgoingMessageClass.html: built by instantiating the class store's OutgoingMessage, then returned from an HTTP handler.

recipes.note: Populate .body, .headers and .status, then return it from an HTTP handler.

sharedSemantics.note: Writes must be enclosed in Use...End use.

Session._reason: SessionClass.html: `Session` is a command returning the session of the current process. Its .storage is a shared object, so writes need Use...End use.

requires: scalable sessions enabled, in a web/REST or remote client process
recipes.note: Returns Null in a process that has no session.
Shortcut to the session's shared .storage object.

sharedSemantics.note: Writes must be enclosed in Use...End use.

Signal._reason: SignalClass.html: New signal creates one; signals are shared objects passed between processes.

recipes.note: Pass it to a worker/process, then .wait() on it in the caller.

SystemWorker._reason: SystemWorkerClass.html: 4D.SystemWorker.new() launches asynchronously; the SystemWorker command runs synchronously and returns a status object instead.

recipes.note: Asynchronous. Call .wait() to block until the process exits.

TCPConnection._reason: TCPConnectionClass.html: 4D.TCPConnection.new(address; port; options) opens the connection.

TCPEvent._reason: TCPEventClass.html: event objects are passed by 4D into the callbacks declared in a TCPConnection's or TCPListener's options.

requires: a TCPConnection or TCPListener with callbacks configured
recipes.note: Supplied by 4D to the callback; cannot be created by user code.

Transporter._reason: Transporter has NO API page — its 11 members are documented only on the IMAP/POP3/SMTP transporter pages. It is a documentation-level base class, in scope so its members are declared once rather than three times.

recipes.note: Transporter is the shared base of IMAPTransporter, POP3Transporter and SMTPTransporter. Obtain one of those.

UDPEvent._reason: UDPEventClass.html: same callback-supplied pattern as TCPEvent.

recipes.note: Supplied by 4D to the callback; cannot be created by user code.

Vector._reason: VectorClass.html: 4D.Vector.new() builds a vector from a collection of numbers, for similarity search.

WebForm._reason: WebFormClass.html: the Web Form command returns the current Qodly page's form object.

recipes.note: Returns Null outside a Qodly page context.

WebFormItem._reason: WebFormItemClass.html: items are reached as named properties of the Web Form object.

requires: a Qodly page containing a component named myButton
recipes._reason: WebFormItemClass.html: items are reached as properties of the Web Form object. No `Web Form Item` command exists in the 21-R3 corpus, so there is no classic-command recipe.

WebServer._reason: WebServerClass.html: WEB Server returns the requested web server object; there is no constructor.

recipes.note: Defaults to the web server of the current context (host database, component, or remote).
Selects a specific web server explicitly.

WebSocket._reason: WebSocketClass.html: 4D.WebSocket.new(url; options) opens a client connection.

recipes.note: This is the WebSocket *client*.

WebSocketConnection._reason: WebSocketConnectionClass.html: supplied by 4D to a WebSocketServer's connection handler.

recipes.note: Server-side view of one client connection; cannot be created by user code.

requires: a user class implementing the connection handler

ZipArchive._reason: ZipArchiveClass.html: archives are opened with ZIP Read archive; ZIP Create archive writes one.

recipes.note: Read-only view; the archive's contents are exposed through .root.

ZipFile._reason: ZipFileClass.html: zip files are reached through an opened archive's root folder; syntaxEN records _inheritedFrom_ Document. The recipe must use .files(), not .file(name): .file() is inherited from Directory and its documented return type is 4D.File, so tool4d rejects `$zipFile:=$archive.root.file("README.md")` with 'Impossible to cast 4D.File to 4D.ZipFile.' (verified against oopcheck/Project via tool4d-lsp-stdio check-syntax).

requires: an archive opened with ZIP Read archive
recipes.note: Read-only. Use .copyTo() to extract before reading with normal File APIs.

ZipFolder._reason: ZipFolderClass.html: the archive's .root is a ZipFolder; syntaxEN records _inheritedFrom_ Directory.

requires: an archive opened with ZIP Read archive

4D._reason: ClassStoreClass.html: `4D` is the built-in class store. It is a language-level namespace, not an instantiable object.

recipes.note: The built-in class store. Its properties are the built-in classes (4D.File, 4D.Blob, ...).

instantiation.note: The class store is a namespace, not an instance. Members are reached as 4D.<Class>.

_orda_templates: Decision 3 of the plan: the ORDA generated classes are modelled as templates, not as per-class command entries. A project with N exposed tables produces 3N generated classes whose members are exactly those of the corresponding built-in base class plus the project's own attributes, so enumerating them per project would be unbounded and project-specific.

cs._reason: ClassStoreClass.html: `cs` is the user class store of the open project. Its properties are the project's own classes plus the ORDA generated classes.

recipes.note: The user class store. Members are project-specific, so this class is a template.

cs.<DataClass>._reason: ORDA generates one dataclass class per exposed table. Its members are exactly 4D.DataClass's, plus nothing table-specific; the table-specific surface is on the entity.

requires: a datastore with an exposed Employee table
recipes.note: Substitute the real table name for <DataClass>.

cs.<DataClass>.templateNote: Members: inherit every member of DataClass. No additional generated members.

cs.<DataClass>Entity._reason: ORDA generates one entity class per exposed table. Its members are 4D.Entity's plus one property per exposed attribute of that table — which is why it is a template rather than an enumerable class.

requires: a datastore with an exposed Employee table
recipes.note: Substitute the real table name for <DataClass>.

requires: a datastore with an exposed Employee table

cs.<DataClass>Entity.templateNote: Members: every member of Entity, plus one dynamic property per exposed attribute (modelled by Entity.attributeName).

cs.<DataClass>Selection._reason: ORDA generates one entity-selection class per exposed table. Members are 4D.EntitySelection's plus one projected property per exposed attribute.

requires: a datastore with an exposed Employee table
recipes.note: Substitute the real table name for <DataClass>.

cs.<DataClass>Selection.templateNote: Members: every member of EntitySelection, plus one dynamic projected property per exposed attribute (modelled by EntitySelection.attributeName).
